title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity — roles, stop, logprobs, streaming & function call formatting
author: Samira Patel
description:
This PR implements OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity across several parameters and output behaviors: roles, stop sequences (including streaming termination), token-level logprobs, and structured/function-call response formatting. Motivation: customers expect drop-in compatibility for clients built against OpenAI's chat completions endpoint; parity reduces migration friction and enables downstream SDKs and examples to work without forks.

What changed (high level):
- Add OpenAI-compatible request parsing and validation for `messages` with roles (system/user/assistant), explicit role coercion rules, and role-presence checks.
- Implement `stop` sequence support for both non-streaming and streaming paths. For streaming, we added an early-stop detector that safely closes streams when stop tokens are observed without emitting truncated JSON objects.
- Expose `logprobs` up to N token positions via the compatibility layer. Non-streaming returns a logprobs object matching OpenAI shape; streaming emits incremental `delta` entries with token+logprob metadata in a stable, backward-compatible envelope.
- Improve structured output & function-calling parity: when `functions` is supplied, we format assistant messages with `role: assistant` and `content` set to the JSON function_call payload in the same shape OpenAI clients expect (including `name` and `arguments` fields). We also ensure `finish_reason` uses the same keywords (e.g. `stop`, `function_call`, `length`).
- Tests: added unit and integration tests, plus golden snapshots using the existing openai-compat harness.
- Docs: added a compatibility doc describing edge cases and behavior differences (docs/openai_chat_parity.md).

Checklist:
- [x] Request parsing for messages+roles
- [x] stop sequences for streaming and non-streaming
- [x] logprobs shape & streaming deltas
- [x] function calling output formatting
- [x] integration tests + snapshots
- [x] small perf smoke tests (throughput/latency baseline)
- [x] docs and changelog entry

Backward compatibility notes: this change lives behind the `openai_compat` endpoint. Existing Redwood endpoints are unaffected. Some subtle differences remain (see docs/openai_chat_parity.md) around multi-byte token boundaries and tokenizer differences; we log those cases and surface warnings when exact parity cannot be guaranteed.

Testing notes: CI initially failed linting for docstrings and one flaky streaming test. I fixed the lint errors and added extra retry logic for the streaming test; CI passed on the final run. Load tests show no CPU regression for typical small-message chat workloads; streaming paths see a small (~3%) memory overhead due to extra metadata buffering for `logprobs` streaming deltas.

Related: ENG-4521, ENG-4599.

Merge: squash merge after approvals and green CI.
